## Goal

Prove on real traffic that the all-opencode off-peak low chain absorbs local-slot overflow, and that it neither widens paid spend outside the windows nor regresses the free tier.

## Work

1. **Baseline** (pre-change window) via the proxy-usage-analysis skill CLI:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`
   Record: `rate_limited`, `fallback_after_queue`, `empty_response`, HTTP 429/503 counts, per-model token share, `munitoai-free` share.
2. After one full 24 h window post-change, re-run the same CLI and diff the same metrics.
3. In `proxy.log`, confirm `Fallback triggered ... to=opencode-go*` events for low-priority traffic occur **only** inside the `available_times` windows, and **zero** inside the UTC 01:00–04:00 / 06:00–10:00 gaps.
4. Confirm the three opencode keys each received traffic (i.e. per-key failover actually engages) by counting dispatches per `entry=` — `opencode-go-3` / `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` map one-to-one to `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. The log line carries `entry=`, not `api_key_env=`.
5. Comment the parent item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX) with the before/after table and verdict, and mirror the table on this item.

## Observation window

- Config change LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I was activated live at **2026-10-19T14:43Z** via `POST /admin/reload-config` (no proxy restart, no llama-server change); the 5-entry low chain has been in effect since.
- Baseline was captured over the 24 h window **2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48** and is recorded in the comments below.
- The post-change measurement needs ≥24 h after activation (i.e. after **2026-10-20T14:43Z**) and must include at least one complete cheap window (01:00–10:00 local = 00:00–09:00 UTC) so low routing is actually exercised.
- Sample-size caveat: the baseline window contained only 13 low-priority sessions, so a single night's post-change sample may be too small to move aggregate rates — report the effect size with that caveat rather than claiming a verified improvement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Before/after metrics table recorded on the parent work item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX) and mirrored on this item, covering `rate_limited`, `fallback_after_queue`, `empty_response`, HTTP 429/503 counts, per-model token share and `munitoai-free` share.
- AC2: Log evidence of at least one low-priority fallback to an opencode entry inside an off-peak window — or a documented reason none occurred (e.g. local never overflowed in that window).
- AC3: **Zero** low-priority opencode fallbacks inside the UTC gap windows (01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00) — proving no paid spend leaked outside permissible times.
- AC4: Per-key dispatch counts (`entry=opencode-go-3` / `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go`) show whether more than one opencode key was used; if only one was used, say whether that reflects no 429s or an unexpected exclusion bug.
- AC5: Explicit cost statement: did paid-tier token share rise outside the overlap hours? Yes = regression, record it.
- AC6: Honest sample-size caveat when the window is too small to move aggregate numbers — state the low-priority dispatch/fallback counts the verdict rests on.

## Evidence commands

```bash
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24 --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy
grep -h "Fallback triggered" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | grep "to=opencode-go"     # window placement
grep -h -o "entry=opencode-go[a-z0-9-]*" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | sort | uniq -c # per-key dispatch
grep -h "priority_routing" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | tail -n 5                    # low chain width (expect providers=5)
```

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 (plan): pre-check returned effort XS / risk Low → full decomposition skipped; six automated review stages run against existing content.
  - AC1 now names the metrics it compares and requires the table mirrored on this item (traces Work 1–2 and 5).
  - Acceptance criteria converted from a numbered list to `- AC1:` … `- AC6:` bullets so `extract_acceptance_criteria()` (shared/tree_coverage.py) and the audit/implement tooling can see them; text unchanged. Heading normalised to `## Acceptance Criteria`.
  - Work 4 corrected: dispatches are counted per `entry=`; the log carries no `api_key_env=` field.
  - Added "Observation window" (activation time, baseline window, ≥24 h plus one complete cheap window).
  - AC6 clarified: the sample size behind the verdict must be stated.
  - Added verified evidence commands (patterns checked against `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`).
  - No child items created: single-session measurement task, a leaf by design (Extra Small effort, Low risk).
data.title: Verify off-peak low-priority fallback in a live window

# Intake Brief: Install the `.githooks/pre-push` gate (core.hooksPath) so the dev-push full-suite gate actually runs

**Headline:** This checkout runs **no** pre-push hook at all (`core.hooksPath` unset, `.git/hooks/pre-push` absent), and the committed hook is the framework **v2** variant which has **no full-suite test gate** — so a red tree can reach `dev`. Close the gap by activating the hook, adding a scope-aware full-suite gate to llm's `.githooks/pre-push` (runner resolved repo-local → global skill path), an idempotent installer, and documentation.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` intentionally defers full-suite testing to the dev-push integration gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81): the `.githooks/pre-push` hook is supposed to run `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on pushes to `dev`/`main`. In this llm checkout neither half is in place:

1. `git config core.hooksPath` is **unset** and `.git/hooks/pre-push` is absent — no hook is invoked at all (verified 2026-10-20).
2. The committed `.githooks/pre-push` is the framework **v2** hook (worklog sync + branch policy + context-budget gate) — it contains **no** full-suite test gate. The v3 gate with the suite gate exists only in SorraAgents and hard-requires a repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, which llm does not ship.

Consequence (evidence in ticket): `implement.py finish` pushed commit `2f922ab9` to `dev` in under a second with no suite execution; the full-suite cache entry appeared only after a manual `run_tests.py --scope full` run.

## Users / stakeholders

- **Framework/agent operators** pushing work to `dev` via `implement.py finish` or `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` — they rely on the push gate to catch full-suite regressions before `dev` is polluted.
- **Audit/verification consumers** (audit runner, post-push verification) that read the full-suite cache entry produced by the gate — a green `dev` after a push is only trustworthy if the gate ran.
- **SorraAgents framework maintainers** — the canonical v3 gate and its docs (SorraAgents repo) are the reference design; llm's fix must stay consistent with the documented per-project policy.

Example user story: "As an operator finishing work item F2, I push to `dev` via `implement.py finish`; a suite-breaking change must be refused at the push so `dev` never holds a red tree, and a feature-branch push must not be slowed by a full-suite run."

## Acceptance Criteria

Pending producer decisions in the Appendix (Q1–Q3); draft wording below reflects the recommended option and updates the original ACs to match reality:

1. **Gate active:** the checkout has the pre-push gate active via an idempotent install (e.g. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` set by a committed installer script), effective for the main checkout and its worktrees.
2. **Full-suite gate on dev push:** a test push to `dev` with a deliberately failing test is **refused** by the hook (verified once, then reverted). The gate runs the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`) when the push targets `refs/heads/dev`/`refs/heads/main`, resolving the runner from repo-local first, then the global skill path `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
3. **Feature branches unblocked:** a test push to a feature branch is not blocked by the suite (runner never invoked; worklog sync and branch-policy/context-budget checks still apply).
4. **Docs:** the install step is documented in this repo's developer docs (new `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` + pointer from `AGENTS.md` per Q2) and is idempotent (safe to re-run; `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL` or equivalent bypass).
5. **Verification/regression:** a committed shell check or runner-driven assertion drives a simulated `dev` push (stdin) and a feature-branch push; asserts the gate refuses a deliberately failing suite (verified once, then reverted) and that feature-branch pushes skip the suite.
6. **Standard:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Standard:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** infrastructure/tooling only — no proxy code changes.
- **No repo-local `skill/` tree in llm** — the v3 hook as written in SorraAgents hard-fails on every dev push here; the runner must be resolved via the global skill path (same fallback pattern the context-budget gate already uses for `measure_context.py`).
- **SorraAgents policy** (docs/dev/context-budget.md, SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM) deliberately gives non-SorraAgents projects the v2 hook **without** the full-suite gate — extending llm's hook to v3-equivalent diverges from that documented convention and needs producer sign-off (Q1).
- **Worktrees:** `implement.py finish` pushes from a worktree; `core.hooksPath` is common-config so one setting covers all worktrees of this checkout, but a fresh clone/wiped `.git/config` loses it → installer must be re-runnable (idempotent).
- **No cross-repo edits without authorisation:** repo boundaries — `skill/`, `command/`, agent-infra dirs in SorraAgents are out of scope for an LP item without explicit direction (affects Q2).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Push timeout vs cold-suite duration:** `implement.py finish` pushes with a 600 s default timeout (`_resolve_test_timeout` → `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand`; llm has no override); on timeout it kills the whole process group and raises `PushTimeoutError` — the code explicitly anticipates the pre-push hook's `run_tests.py` outliving the parent. A cold ~4300-test full suite may exceed 600 s on this host, making the gate backfire on the first push after the cache expires (2 h TTL, git-state fingerprint). **Mitigation (recommended):** provision a sensible per-command timeout (or pre-warm the suite cache) in the same work item; verify with a timed simulated push. The 2 h cache makes repeat pushes cheap.
- **Cache location in worktrees:** pushes originate from worktrees; the runner writes `.worklog/cache` under its invocation repo. Implement's post-push/audit consumers read main-checkout `.worklog/cache` — a worktree-cached run may be invisible to them unless run cwd/cache resolution matches (verify; may need to run the gate from the main checkout or confirm the runner resolves the repo root consistently).
- **`--strict-git-env`:** the runner refuses to run when repository-override env (`GIT_DIR` etc.) is present; if any wrapper injects these, the gate would hard-fail or need `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP`. Verify in the simulated push.
- **Divergence from framework policy:** extending the llm hook to a v3-equivalent full-suite gate contradicts the documented sibling-project convention (SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM gives siblings v2 without the suite gate). Producer sign-off required (Q1); if declined, AC2 cannot be met by a hook-only fix and the alternative (framework-side change in `implement.py finish`) is a SorraAgents-scoped item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no proxy code changes; the `.githooks/post-*` hooks and `worklog-post-pull` are out of scope. Any discovered framing improvements (e.g. installing the hook on sibling repos, updating SorraAgents docs table) are recorded as linked work items, not folded into this one.
- **Assumption:** `implement.py finish` pushes without `--no-verify` (verified — no `--no-verify` in the push path), so an active hook gate applies to framework pushes, not just manual ones.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` committed (v2, file mtime 2026-08-31): worklog pre-push sync (branch `refs/worklog/data`), protected-branch policy (`main`/`master`/`HEAD`), context-budget regression gate (F6) — **no** test gate.
- `git config core.hooksPath` → unset; `.git/hooks/pre-push` → absent (only `*.sample`).
- Global test runner present: `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (the runner `/skill:test` uses; supports `--scope full --strict-git-env`, and caches results per git state in `.worklog/cache`).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` exists in llm (total 967) — context-budget gate is satisfiable.
- llm has no `docs/dev/release-process.md` (the dev-push-gate docs live in SorraAgents); llm has `docs/dev/` with other analysis docs.
- `.git/config` `[core]` section shows no `hooksPath` line; repo has ~82 worktrees sharing the common config.

## Desired change

1. Add a scope-aware full-suite gate to llm's `.githooks/pre-push` (v3-equivalent): read stdin once, capture push targets; `need_full_suite` when `remote_ref` is `refs/heads/dev|main`; run the runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env --json`; refuse the push on failure; skip tests for feature-branch pushes (matching SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 semantics). Runner resolution: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first, then global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (mirrors the existing `measure_context.py` resolution); fail behaviour on "no runner found" per Q3.
2. Idempotent installer (`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`): set `core.hooksPath=.githooks`; leave committed hooks untouched (never overwrite); `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1` bypass.
3. Docs: new `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (install, verify: `git config --get core.hooksPath`; simulate dev push via stdin) + pointer from `AGENTS.md` (per Q2).
4. Verification test: a shell check or runner-driven assertion that a simulated `dev` push invokes the gate and a feature-branch push skips it.

## Key Files

- `.githooks/pre-push` — add scope-aware full-suite gate (v3-equivalent with global-runner fallback)
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — new idempotent installer (sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, skip flag)
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — new developer doc (install, verify, bypass knobs) (location per Q2)
- `AGENTS.md` — pointer line to the hook install doc (location per Q2)
- Reference: SorraAgents `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, canonical gate implementation) — read-only reference, not to be edited from an LP item

## Related work

- SorraAgents SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 — full-suite testing deferred to the dev-push integration gate (the design this item implements for llm).
- SorraAgents SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 — scope-aware test gate (v3 hook).
- SorraAgents SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM — per-project hook-variant selection (siblings ship v2, no suite gate) — the policy Q1 asks to extend.
- SorraAgents SA-0MT1WPMFY002N71Z — v2 pre-push hook with context-budget gate (source of llm's current hook).
- LP-0MUFJQ8ON009URQL — completed `[test-failure]` for `test-pre-push-hook.mjs` (SorraAgents hook test; confirms v3 semantics: dev push without repo-local runner hard-fails).
- LP-0MUHOHP82006NT3W — completed item on committed symlinks causing duplicate/inconsistent test collection in worktrees (caveat against a `skill/` symlink approach for runner resolution; prefer global-path fallback).
- Duplicate check performed (2026-10-20): `wl search` for `pre-push`, `hooksPath`, `hook`, `test gate`, `dev-push` — no overlapping open/completed item covers llm's hook installation; proceed.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (OPEN QUESTION): **Where should the full-suite gate live for llm?** The committed llm hook is v2 (no test gate) and the v3 gate assumes a repo-local runner llm lacks. Options: (a) **Recommended** — extend llm's `.githooks/pre-push` to a v3-equivalent gate with runner resolution repo-local → global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; self-contained, satisfies all four original ACs. (b) Keep llm on v2 and instead fix `implement.py finish` (SorraAgents) to run the full suite before pushing — contradicts SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81's deliberate deferral and is cross-repo. (c) Symlink/create a repo-local `skill/` tree and install the unmodified v3 hook — risks duplicate test collection (LP-0MUHOHP82006NT3W) and ships a framework tree into llm.
- Q2 (OPEN QUESTION): **Where are the install docs published?** llm has no `docs/dev/release-process.md`; gate docs live in SorraAgents. Options: (a) **Recommended** — new `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` + `AGENTS.md` pointer in llm (self-contained, satisfies "documented in developer docs" within repo scope). (b) Update SorraAgents `docs/dev/context-budget.md` project table + rollout section — cross-repo edit under an LP item; needs a SorraAgents work item. (c) Both.
- Q3 (OPEN QUESTION): **Fail behaviour when the test runner cannot be found on a dev/main push** (e.g. fresh machine without pi skill install). Options: (a) **Recommended** — fail-closed (refuse the push), matching v3 semantics and the ticket's "deterministic" intent; deterministic gate, at the cost that a machine without the global skill cannot push to dev until it runs the installer. (b) Fail-open with a loud warning (mirrors the context-budget gate's fail-open when `measure_context.py` is absent); keeps pushes working but re-opens the incident's hole on un-provisioned machines.

## Effort and risk (pre-decision estimate)

- **Effort: M (medium).** Rough WBS for the recommended option (Q1a): hook gate edit (~80 lines shell, mirroring v3), installer script (~30 lines), 1 shell/runner-driven verification test, docs (~1 page) → O=2 h, M=4 h, P=8 h.
- **Risk: Medium.** Drivers: (i) cold full-suite duration vs the 600 s push timeout (highest-impact unknown — a slow gate could break every `implement.py finish` push); (ii) divergence from the documented sibling-project hook policy; (iii) cache visibility from worktrees. Mitigations: timed simulated push with a provisioned `timeoutPerCommand`, keep the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` escape hatch, choose fail-closed only after Q3.
- **Contingent on Q1:** option (b) (framework-side change in `implement.py finish`, SorraAgents) is out of LP scope and would be a separate cross-repo item; option (c) (repo-local `skill/` symlink + stock v3 hook) raises the risk to High given the known duplicate-collection defect (LP-0MUHOHP82006NT3W).
- **Confidence:** 60% on effort, driven by the unresolved timeout question. Re-run `/skill:effort-and-risk` after Q1–Q3 are answered (script requires stage `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MUFJQ8ON009URQL** – [test-failure] tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs::BRANCH_POLICY_SKIP=1 bypasses the policy check — failing test (completed)
- **LP-0MV7WUEJW0033UAN** – Close coverage gap: **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (completed)
- **LP-0MRNV040H0055N2Q** – [test-failure] test_stub_router_integration — flaky test-ordering-dependent assert ok Failure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac2, acceptance, acs, active (+339 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, ac2, acceptance, acs, active (+339 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, ac2, acceptance, acs, active (+339 more)

# Intake brief: make local GPU utilisation/prefill metrics visible to the usage report

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy usage report to measure **local prefill time**
(dispatch → first byte) alongside decode time, so "GPU busy %" reflects real slot
occupancy and large local prompts stop being invisible.

## Problem statement

`report.md` currently reports `Local model utilization → Busy time = 7h 02m (29.3%)`
and `Total compute (slot-time) = 7h 47m`, derived by pairing **local `Stream
started` → `Stream finished`**. That window starts at *first byte*, so the entire
prefill/prompt-processing phase is excluded.

For large local prompts, prefill is the dominant cost. In the same 24h window
(2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23) the proxy logged `dispatch_first_byte_ms` for
every one of the **463** local requests:

| Prefill (dispatch → first byte) | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Samples | 463 |
| p10 | 3.3 s |
| **median** | **61.8 s** |
| p90 | 269.8 s |
| max | 817 s (13.6 min) |
| **Sum** | **14.3 h** |

Examples: `dispatch_first_byte_ms=98697.8 cache_state=warm cached_ratio=0.942` and
`dispatch_first_byte_ms=133126.9 cache_state=cold cached_ratio=0.000` (212 cold /
251 warm in the window). Adding 14.3 h of prefill to 7 h 47 m of decode puts real
occupancy near **79,500 s ≈ 46% of 48 slot-hours**, versus the 16% the report
implies. This directly misleads capacity work (slot count, ctx size, queue
tuning) — including the concurrent slot-count investigation.

Corroborating gaps in the same report:

- `## Decode speed` and `## Prompt eval speed` are **empty** ("No llama-server eval
  timing samples in window"), so there is no independent decode/prefill evidence.
  `llama-server.log*` in the window contains no `eval time` lines (older rotated
  files do, e.g. `llama-server.log-2026-10-07.gz` has 296) — ingestion or build
  verbosity likely regressed, and that must be established.
- The report's TTFT table is dominated by remote samples; local `ttft_seconds` is
  never logged (only `dispatch_first_byte_ms`).
- The prefill phase is observable in the proxy already: 11,050
  `lease_extended_during_prefill` events with `progress=None`, i.e. prefill polling
  works but exposes no numeric progress.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `proxy-usage-analysis` computes and reports **local prefill time** per local
   stream from `dispatch_first_byte_ms` (falling back to the pairing of dispatch
   and first byte when absent), including p10/p50/p90/max and the **window total**,
   with an explicit statement that the figure is slot-time, not wall-clock.
2. `Local model utilization` reports `busy` as the union of
   **dispatch → finish** intervals (prefill + decode), with the decode-only figure
   retained alongside as a separate row, and a labelled lower/upper bound. Existing
   fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats keep working on the new intervals.
3. A `Prefill vs decode` breakdown appears in the report (slot-seconds and % of
   slot-time each), so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes.
4. The empty decode/prompt-eval sections are fixed or explained automatically:
   determine why no llama-server eval-timing samples exist in the current window
   (`llama-server.log` verbosity / build / rotation) and either restore ingestion
   or have the report print a named, self-diagnosing reason (log path, files
   scanned, lines matched) instead of an unattributed blank.
5. Unit tests cover: the prefill parser, the union-interval busy calculation
   (including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams), the fast/cheap split on
   the new intervals, and the empty-eval-timing diagnostic path. Fixtures are
   copied from real `/var/log/llama-proxy` lines (`dispatch_first_byte_ms=`).
6. A regenerated report for the same window shows the corrected busy figure and
   the new prefill/decode split, with the numbers in this brief used as the
   expected-order sanity check (≈14.3 h prefill, ≈7.8 h decode).

## Risks / notes

- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` is logged per local request but is **not** identical to
  `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` (queue wait is split out as `queue_wait_ms`); define
  which interval maps to slot occupancy and document it.
- Unfinished/aborted local streams (2 in the window) have no `dispatch_first_byte_ms`;
  they must be reported as "unknown prefill" rather than silently dropped.
- Changing "busy" semantics changes historical comparability; keep the old
  decode-only number visible and state the definition change in the report header.
data.title: Make local GPU busy/prefill metrics visible in the proxy usage report

# Run the controlled N=3 (and N=4) slot-count sweep in a quiet/maintenance window

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the measured N=3/N=4 sweep that
`LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` could not complete on shared production, so the
concurrency-vs-capacity projection (N=2 denies ~19.7% of session-minutes;
N=3 ~6.7%) is validated or refuted against real local TTFT, decode speed,
queue-timeout rate and VRAM.

## Why this exists

The deterministic analysis in `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`
(AC1/AC2/AC4) is complete and recommends **keep N=2** pending this sweep. The
AC3 measured sweep was attempted on 2026-10-20 against the live proxy while it
was serving 5 concurrent sessions (52 distinct sessions / 5 min, 2 audits + 4
herdr panes holding local leases). Every benchmark turn-1 request stalled at
600–760 s (1200 s timeout) and llama-server stopped answering health probes, so
the run was aborted, the harness restored the config (sha256 `6eec5656…`) and a
controlled `start-proxy.sh --restart` returned the proxy to healthy (N=2,
`--parallel 2`).

## Task

Run the sweep in a window with no other local-lease holders (drain or stop
herdr panes / audits), using the same harness as the prior verdict
(`LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7` / `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`):

```
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>
# then, if memory permits:
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --slots 4 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>
```

Record per N: local TTFT (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`), decode tok/s,
queue-timeout rate, denials, `finish_reason=length` count, llama-server
startup + `--parallel` agreement (must match `session_slot_pool_size`), per-slot
KV memory and system MemAvailable. Then update the decision in
`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (or a successor doc) and,
if the verdict moves to N=3/N=4, create the config-change item that also
re-decides the warm-threshold = 95%-of-per-slot target (which becomes 79,121 at
N=3 vs 120,627 at N=2).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A sweep run at N=2, N=3 (and N=4 if memory allows) with the harness above,
   with the results committed under `proxy/benchmarks/results/`.
2. The run records `--parallel` agreement, per-slot context clamp, and system
   MemAvailable, and explicitly notes any validity caveat (live leases, remote
   fallback) as the prior verdict did.
3. A recorded verdict (keep N=2 / move to N=3 / N=4) that reconciles the
   measured queue-timeout and denial rates with the concurrency projection in
   the reevaluation doc.

## Risks / notes

- N=3 clamps per-slot context to 83,285 (warm threshold 79,121); N=4 to 61,440.
- Prefill is serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), so more slots add
  decode concurrency, not prefill capacity.
- Do **not** run this against the shared proxy during active multi-agent work.

data.description:
## Goal

Explain and, if it is a defect, fix the single `available_times` gate bypass observed while verifying LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO, so paid opencode spend can never happen inside the UTC gap windows (01:00-04:00, 06:00-10:00).

Discovered from: LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO (verification of LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX — off-peak low-priority fallback).

## Observation

In the post-change 24 h window (2026-10-20 14:44:27 - 2026-10-21 14:44:27 local = 13:44 - 13:44 UTC) there was exactly **one** low-priority fallback to an opencode entry inside a forbidden gap window, at **2026-10-21 01:00:05 UTC** (`log` 02:00:05 local):

```
2026-10-21 02:00:05,162 Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
2026-10-21 02:00:05,162 Skipping provider=opencode-go: quota_exhausted (account=OPENCODE_API_KEY, ...)
2026-10-21 02:00:05,162 Fallback triggered ... from=munitoai-free, to=opencode-go-3, reason=rate_limited
2026-10-21 02:00:05,163 Stream started: provider=OpenCode Go 3 ... entry=opencode-go-3
```

Two seconds earlier (01:00:03 UTC) the same chain correctly logged `Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: outside its available_times window (UTC)` for another request, so the gate is not simply disabled for `-3`. Note that `opencode-go-3`'s skip line is **absent** in the 01:00:05 sequence — the third entry was reached already having "passed" eligibility.

Impact: 2 dispatches / 52,329 tokens (0.006% of the window's 828.5M logged tokens) — small, but the gap-window invariant is supposed to be absolute.

## Hypothesis (needs confirmation)

`_select_provider`-style loops call `_provider_in_allowed_window(provider_cfg, config)` with no explicit `now_utc`, so the gate reads the clock at evaluation time; but the request appears to have been in flight/across the 01:00 UTC boundary. Alternatively one path (e.g. the pre-existing in-flight/retry path or the 429-failover sibling hop) re-enters the chain without re-running the `available_times` gate — the surge-bypass helper `_provider_in_allowed_window` could also have reported True during a window edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Root cause identified and documented on this item with a log-derived reproduction (specific code path, and why `opencode-go-3`'s skip line was absent).
- AC2: A regression test covers the identified path and fails before the fix.
- AC3: If it is a defect, the fix guarantees no opencode dispatch outside `available_times` unless the documented final-week quota-surge bypass (LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8) applies to that account.
- AC4: A post-fix verification statement records zero gap-window opencode dispatches over a full cheap window.
data.title: Investigate available_times gate bypass for opencode-go-3 at 01:00:05 UTC (2 dispatches in gap window)

## Full 24 h before/after measurement (from LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO) — chain works; one 2-dispatch gap leak filed as a bug

This is the 24 h comparison the parent's AC8 deferred. Full detail, caveats and per-AC verdicts: **LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO**.

Windows (log clock = local Europe/Dublin, UTC+1; the 5-entry low chain went live at 2026-10-19 14:44:27 local = **13:44:27 UTC**, i.e. the description's "14:43Z" was a local-time stamp):

- Baseline: 2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48 (24 h, pre-change)
- Post-change: 2026-10-20 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 14:44:27 (24 h, one complete cheap window)

| Metric | Baseline | Post-change | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions / requests | 217 / 12,810 | 228 / 9,137 | |
| Fallback events | 11,654 (91.0%) | 8,405 (92.0%) | −3,249 |
| `rate_limited` | 4,733 (40.6%) | 3,629 (43.2%) | −1,104 |
| `fallback_after_queue` | 1,868 | 149 | **−1,719** |
| `empty_response` | 58 | 128 | +70 |
| HTTP 429 (fallback reason) | 16 | 36 | +20 |
| HTTP 503 (fallback reason) | 93 | 24 | −69 |
| Upstream 429 / 502 / 503 | 16 / 1 / 1 (all `api.munito.ai`) | 61 / 0 / 26 (`opencode-go` 60 / 0 / 25) | |
| Logged tokens | 421.7 M | 828.5 M | +96% |
| Per-model share (session-attributed) | MunitoAI 43.1%, OpenCode 36.2%, local 10.6%, opencode-go 10.1% | OpenCode 69.6%, MunitoAI 20.1%, local 10.3% | |
| `munitoai-free` share | 43.1% (row groups free+paid) | 20.1% | −23.0 pts |
| Local streams / `munitoai*` entry lines / `opencode-go-3` dispatches | 910 / 14,555 / 9,242 | 576 / 5,967 / 11,106 | −37% / −59% / +20% |

Low-priority outcome (cheap window = 01:00–10:00 local; opencode windows leave only 01:00–02:00 and 05:00–07:00 local inside it):

- **915** low-priority fallbacks into `opencode-go-3`/`-2` inside those permitted overlap hours (904 `munitoai-free → opencode-go-3`, 10 `local-qwen3 → opencode-go-3`, 1 → `-2`), 1,806 dispatches, **137.2 M paid tokens** — the overflow absorption this epic was built for. Baseline: **0** opencode dispatches in cheap hours (`priority_routing priority=low providers=2` then).
- **Gap windows** (UTC 01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00): **1** fallback / **2** dispatches / 52.3 k tokens (0.006% of the window) at 2026-10-21 01:00:05 UTC — not literally zero, so the strict "zero leakage" wording is unmet. A single boundary event, filed as **LP-0MVI9TXIZ0077PZV**.
- **Per-key failover confirmed:** `opencode-go-3` 11,106 dispatches, `opencode-go-2` 30 (`OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` engaged after account-3 rate limits), `opencode-go` 0 — only because that account had `quota_exhausted` headroom 0.0% in this window (resets ≈2026-10-23), not because of an exclusion bug. Over 48 h all three keys served traffic (`-3` 18,995, `-2` 30, `-1` 13,817).
- **Cost:** paid tokens inside the overlap windows 16.6% of logged tokens; in the gaps 0.006%; the paid share of logged tokens did not rise (it is ~100% in both windows — local and `munitoai-free` streams emit no `tokens=` triple, so they never enter a token share). Absolute token volume rose +96% but seven other config/code changes landed inside the window, so that is not attributable to this epic. The 48 h gap-hour volume (196 M tokens) is the documented final-week **quota-surge bypass** for `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8), which is designed to lift `available_times`.

**Verdict:** the all-opencode off-peak low chain works as designed — it absorbs low-priority overflow only inside the permitted windows, per-key failover engages, and the free tier's relative share fell 59% in entry terms. Two findings to carry forward: the single boundary-event gap leak (bug filed) and the window-blind aggregate token-volume rise (separate cost trend, not this change).

## Measurement complete — verdict: change works inside its windows; one 2-dispatch leak in a gap window

### Windows measured

| | Window (log clock = **local** Europe/Dublin, UTC+1 in Oct) | UTC equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (pre-change) | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48 | 13:37 → 13:37 |
| Post-change, 24 h | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | 13:44 → 13:44 |
| Post-change, 48 h (secondary) | 2026-10-19 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 15:20:00 | 13:44 → 14:20 |

**Activation timestamp correction:** `proxy.log` timestamps are **local**, not UTC. The first `priority_routing ... priority=low providers=5` line is **2026-10-19 14:44:27 local = 13:44:27 UTC**, not 14:43Z as the description states (the 14:43 stamp was already local). The 5-entry low chain has been live since then — 48 h before this measurement.

The 24 h post-change window is the comparable one: fully post-activation, fully logged, and contains one complete cheap window (2026-10-21 01:00–10:00 local = 00:00–09:00 UTC). The 48 h window is used only for the per-key evidence (AC4); it contains a **6 h 24 m log gap** (2026-10-20 06:46 → 13:10 local, proxy restart), so its aggregates under-cover and are not used for the before/after comparison.

Command (reproducible):

```bash
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
  --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --start "2026-10-20 14:44:27" --end "2026-10-21 14:44:27" \
  --output-dir /tmp/lpverify/post24
```

### AC1 — before/after metrics table

| Metric | Baseline 24 h | Post-change 24 h | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions | 217 | 228 | +11 |
| Requests | 12,810 (local 908 / remote 11,902) | 9,137 (local 577 / remote 8,560) | −3,673 |
| Fallback events | 11,654 (91.0%) | 8,405 (92.0%) | −3,249 |
| `rate_limited` | 4,733 (40.6%) | 3,629 (43.2%) | −1,104 |
| `fallback_after_queue` | 1,868 | 149 | **−1,719** |
| `empty_response` | 58 | 128 | +70 |
| `context_too_large` | 3,320 | 568 | −2,752 |
| `provider_context_exceeded` | — (not emitted pre-change) | 2,003 | new |
| `large_context_bypass` | 1,322 | 832 | −490 |
| HTTP 429 (fallback reason) | 16 | 36 | +20 |
| HTTP 503 (fallback reason) | 93 | 24 | −69 |
| Upstream HTTP 429 (error events) | 16 — **all** `api.munito.ai` | 61 — `opencode-go` 60, `api.munito.ai` 1 | +45 |
| Upstream HTTP 502 / 503 | 1 / 1 (`api.munito.ai`) | 0 / 26 (`opencode-go` 25, `api.munito.ai` 1) | |
| Logged tokens (input+output) | 421.7 M | 828.5 M | +96% |
| Token share by model (session-initial attribution) | MunitoAI 43.1%, OpenCode 36.2%, local 10.6%, opencode-go 10.1% | OpenCode 69.6%, MunitoAI 20.1%, local 10.3% | |
| `munitoai-free` row share | not separable in this table (the `MunitoAI` row groups free + paid) → 43.1% | 20.1% | **−23.0 pts** |
| Token share by **serving entry** (log-derived) | `opencode-go-3` 99.98%, `opencode-go-2` 0.02% | `opencode-go-3` 99.36%, `opencode-go-2` 0.20%, `deepseek-flash` 0.44% | |
| Local streams | 910 | 576 | −37% |
| `munitoai-free` + `munitoai` entry lines | 14,555 | 5,967 | −59% |
| `opencode-go-3` dispatch lines | 9,242 | 11,106 | +20% |

Two caveats on the token rows, both material:

1. The per-model table groups by the **session's initial provider**, not by the entry that served the tokens — so it is a workload-attribution view, not a spend view.
2. Only opencode/deepseek streams emit a `tokens=prompt/completion/total` triple; **local and munitoai-free streams do not**, so they cannot appear in any token-share row. Every token share above is therefore a share of *paid-serving* tokens. Free-tier share must be read from counts (local streams −37%, munitoai lines −59%), which is what the count rows give.

### AC2 — low-priority fallback to an opencode entry inside an off-peak window: **met**

During the cheap priority window (`server.priority_window` 01:00–10:00 local) every request is capped to `low` (`priority_decision priority=low header=(none|high)`), so all cheap-window traffic is low-priority. The opencode `available_times` windows (UTC) leave only local hours **01:00–02:00** and **05:00–07:00** inside the cheap window.

- **915** fallbacks to an opencode entry in those overlap hours: 904 `munitoai-free → opencode-go-3`, 10 `local-qwen3 → opencode-go-3`, 1 `munitoai-free → opencode-go-2`.
- 1,808 opencode dispatches during cheap-window hours, **1,806 of them inside the permitted overlap windows**.
- First example: `2026-10-21 01:00:16 local (00:00:16 UTC) Fallback triggered ... from=munitoai-free, to=opencode-go-3, reason=provider_context_exceeded`.
- Baseline for contrast: **0** opencode dispatches during cheap-window hours (the pre-change 2-entry low chain ended at `munitoai-free`), and `priority_routing priority=low providers=2` — so the new capacity is demonstrably what absorbs the overflow, not a pre-existing path.

Chain width is live as designed: `priority_routing model=unknown priority=low providers=5` (2,237 occurrences in the window).

### AC3 — zero low-priority opencode fallbacks in the UTC gap windows: **NOT strictly met (1 event)**

Gap hours (local 02:00–05:00 and 07:00–11:00 = UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00), post-change 24 h window:

| Gap hour (local) | Opencode fallbacks | Opencode dispatches |
|---|---|---|
| 10-21 02:00 | **1** | **2** |
| 10-21 03:00, 04:00, 07:00, 08:00, 09:00, 10:00 | 0 | 0 |

Zero everywhere except one event at **2026-10-21 01:00:05 UTC** (02:00:05 local), 52,329 tokens (0.006% of the window's logged tokens):

```
02:00:03 Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: outside its available_times window (UTC)   <- other request, gate works
02:00:05 Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
02:00:05 Skipping provider=opencode-go: quota_exhausted (account=OPENCODE_API_KEY, ...)
02:00:05 Fallback triggered ... from=munitoai-free, to=opencode-go-3, reason=rate_limited
02:00:05 Stream started: provider=OpenCode Go 3 ... entry=opencode-go-3
```

Notice `opencode-go-3`'s skip line is **absent** in that sequence although the same entry was skipped two seconds earlier — the gate is not disabled for `-3`, so this is a per-request eligibility/bypass path worth a look. Filed as **LP-0MVI9TXIZ0077PZV** (bug, discovered-from this item) rather than fixed here, since this item is measurement-only.

So the honest statement is: **no systemic leakage** (1 event, 0.1% of the window's 5,572 opencode fallbacks, 2 dispatches) but not literally zero. AC3 as written ("zero") is therefore unmet; the intent (paid spend confined to permissible times) holds to within 0.006% of tokens.

### AC4 — per-key dispatch counts: **more than one key used; no exclusion bug**

Post-change 24 h window, dispatches by `entry=`:

| Entry | API key | Dispatches | Skips observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode-go-3` | `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` | **11,106** | outside window 924, cooldown 31, same-failure-domain 3 |
| `opencode-go-2` | `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` | **30** (15 fallbacks) | outside window 925, cooldown 2, same-failure-domain 197 |
| `opencode-go` | `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | **0** | `quota_exhausted` 937, same-failure-domain 200 |

- Failover to a second account **does** engage (`-2` served 30 requests, 14 of them after a `munitoai-free` rate-limit). The low count reflects the small number of account-3 429s (36 `HTTP 429` fallback reasons; 60 upstream 429s from `opencode-go`), not an exclusion bug.
- The third key's **zero** is explained by quota state, not by exclusion: every visit logged `Skipping provider=opencode-go: quota_exhausted (account=OPENCODE_API_KEY, effective_headroom=0.0%, resets_in≈200,600 s)` (reset ≈2026-10-23).
- Over the 48 h secondary window all three keys did receive traffic — `-3` 18,995, `-2` 30, `opencode-go` 13,817 — which confirms the third key is reachable when it has headroom (see the surge note below).

### AC5 — cost statement: **no low-chain-driven rise in paid spend outside the overlap hours**

- **Inside** the permissible overlap windows: 137.2 M paid tokens (16.6% of the window's logged tokens) via 915 fallbacks / 1,806 dispatches — this is the change doing exactly what it was built to do.
- **Inside the forbidden gap windows**: 52.3 k paid tokens (0.006%), one event (see AC3). Baseline: 0.
- **Absolute paid volume rose** (421.7 M → 828.5 M logged tokens, +96%) while **requests fell** (12,810 → 9,137), i.e. tokens per request ≈2.8×. Of the logged tokens, 100% were served by paid entries in **both** windows (baseline `opencode-go-3` 99.98% + `-2` 0.02%; post `-3` 99.36% + `-2` 0.20% + `deepseek-flash` 0.44%), so the *paid share of logged tokens did not rise* — the denominator grew.
- That growth cannot be attributed to LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I: **seven other config/code changes landed inside the observation window** (`42f93580`, `f496626e` local admission/prefill; `c443240c`, `ec5514fc`, `242d03f4`, `6999492a`, `a8b56995`), and the proxy was restarted at 2026-10-20 13:10 local. Track the token-volume trend separately; it is not a regression of this change.
- **One documented exception to window discipline, not a regression:** in the 48 h window the `OPENCODE_API_KEY` account entered the final-week **quota-surge bypass** (`quota_surge_bypass entered provider=opencode-go account=OPENCODE_API_KEY resets_at=2026-10-23T08:43:55Z`, 2026-10-20 01:00 UTC; feature LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8, `quota_surge_enabled: true`, `quota_surge_days: 7`). That lift is purposeful use-it-or-lose-it spend at any hour and accounts for the 196 M gap-hour tokens / 3,255 dispatches in the 48 h window. It is independent of the 5-entry low chain.

### AC6 — sample-size caveat and the counts the verdict rests on

- Low-priority sample: **2,202** request-level `priority_decision priority=low` in the 24 h window (23.5% of 9,380 decisions; of these 2,037 had no `X-Priority` header, 165 carried a spoofed `high` that was correctly capped, 2 were explicit `low`). Baseline: 2,257. The request-level sample is **comparable**, not thin.
- The verdict nevertheless rests on modest absolute numbers and I state them: **915** overlap-window opencode fallbacks (AC2), **1** gap-window fallback / 2 dispatches / 52.3 k tokens (AC3), **30 / 0** dispatches on accounts `-2` / `-1` (AC4). One night's cheap window is enough to show the mechanism engages, not enough to estimate a steady-state paid-spend rate — do not read the 16.6% overlap token figure as a recurring cost.
- `low_priority_sessions` from the CLI reads **0** in both post-change windows and 13 in the baseline: that column buckets by the retired fast/cheap **mode schedule**, which the config no longer defines (cheap hours are now a priority cap, not a mode). Use `priority_routing`/`priority_decision` counts instead — which is what this report does.
- Aggregate `rate_limited` (−23%) and `fallback_after_queue` (−92%) moved favourably, `empty_response` (+70) and upstream 503 (+25, all `opencode-go`) moved unfavourably; with seven other changes in-window these deltas are **not** attributable to the low-chain change alone.

### Verdict

The 5-entry low chain **does** absorb low-priority overflow into `opencode-go-3`/`-2` inside the off-peak windows (915 fallbacks, 1,806 dispatches, 137.2 M tokens), does **not** widen paid spend in the gap windows beyond one boundary event (2 dispatches, 0.006% of tokens — bug filed), per-key failover is exercised (`-2` used; `-1` blocked only by exhausted quota), and the free tier's relative share fell as designed (`munitoai-free` lines −59%) without any evidence of a low-chain cost leak.

Verification evidence and the full before/after table live on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO (comment LP-C0MVI9W3A3005433R). Reproduce the single event with: `grep -h '02:00:0[0-9]' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_21 | grep -E 'Skipping|Fallback triggered|Stream started'` — note proxy.log timestamps are LOCAL (Europe/Dublin, UTC+1 in October), so 02:00:05 local = 01:00:05 UTC.

Also worth checking while investigating: the same short-circuit can explain why `opencode-go-3`'s skip line is missing from the sequence (the loop reached the entry already marked eligible).
